name: DHT11 temperature & humidity sensor (bare 4-pin)
description: Aosong DHT11 basic temperature (±2 °C) and relative humidity (±5 %RH) sensor with a single-wire digital output, 1 °C / 1 %RH resolution, read at most every 2 s. Runs on 3.3–5.5 V; DATA needs an external pull-up resistor (10 kΩ, or 4.7 kΩ per the datasheet for long cables). Sold as: Adafruit DHT11 basic temperature-humidity sensor + extras (#386), bare blue 4-pin Aosong DHT11 (pins VCC, DATA, NC, GND) with a loose pull-up resistor.
eli5: A little blue box with four legs that tells your board roughly how warm and how damp the air is, over one wire. It needs one resistor to help it talk.

pins.name: DATA
pins.description: Pin 2: single-wire bidirectional data; needs a pull-up resistor to VCC

buildNotes: Pins 1-4 from the left with the grille facing you: VCC, DATA, NC, GND. Leave pin 3 (NC) unconnected.
Fit a pull-up from DATA to VCC: 10 kΩ is fine on a breadboard; the Aosong datasheet recommends 4.7 kΩ for cables up to 5 m. Without it reads fail with OSError.
Wire DATA to a GPIO that can output as well as input (not GPIO 34-39 on an ESP32).

Use MicroPython's built-in dht module: dht.DHT11(Pin(n)), then measure() and temperature()/humidity(). It sends the 18 ms start pulse, reads the 40 bits and checks the checksum; a bad checksum or no answer raises OSError.
Wait 1 s after power-up, then read no more often than every 2 s. Each reading is the result of the previous measurement, so after a long pause the first value is stale.
On 3.3 V keep the wires short. Readings are whole numbers; use it for 0-50 °C (MicroPython's DHT11 class does not decode the sub-zero sign bit). For better accuracy use a DHT22/AM2302.
Hand-solder at no more than 300 °C for under 3 s; no wave soldering and no cleaning liquids.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import dht, time

sensor = dht.DHT11(Pin({DATA}))
time.sleep(1)  # DHT11 needs 1 s after power-up
while True:
    try:
        sensor.measure()
        print('T=%dC H=%d%%' % (sensor.temperature(), sensor.humidity()))
    except OSError as e:
        print('DHT11 read failed:', e)
    time.sleep(2)  # DHT11: at most one reading every 2 s

test.title: Reports the temperature and humidity set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (2 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
